title: Anan'iv–Bohorodchany cluster (P1481 vs P1485): UNRESOLVED — genuine, well-sourced ambiguity between one trunk under two partial names and two independently built parallel lines

rows.recommendation: Do NOT fold or delete yet — the duplicate question is genuinely unresolved on sourcing (see cluster notes). Independently, FIX the length field: 333.00 km is geometrically impossible for the stated endpoints. Ananiv (Odesa Oblast, ~47.73°N 30.00°E) to Bohorodchany (Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, ~48.80°N 24.51°E) are ~424 km apart on a great circle, so no pipeline route between them can be only 333 km; a pipe is always ≥ the straight-line distance between its own endpoints. Chase where '333' originated (it matches neither the 532.6 km whole-K-A-B-trunk figure nor Moldovatransgaz's own 184.8 km Moldovan-territory-portion figure for the same-named АЧБ trunk) — it looks like a transcription error or a conflation with an unrelated segment length, and should be corrected or the row's true extent re-examined regardless of how the duplicate question resolves. Next step to actually close the duplicate question: get a verbatim (non-WAF-blocked) copy of the Ukrtransgaz historical chronology (utg.ua) and the Bohorodchanske LVUMG chronology page (tsoua.com) — both 403 automated fetches and have no Wayback capture; try a different egress IP, a library/archival route, or ask GEM's Ukraine contacts directly. A single unstable, non-reproducing search-engine synthesis of the tsoua.com page claimed Ukrtransgaz's chronology names TWO separately-commissioned 1987-88 pipelines ('Kremenchuk-Ananiev-Chernivtsi' and 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany') distinct from the 1986 'Kremenchuk-Ananiev-Bohorodchany' — if that specific claim can be verified verbatim, it would REFUTE the duplicate hypothesis (parallel Soviet-era strings, same pattern as the Kazakhstan precedent). A repeat search on the same terms failed to reproduce that claim, so treat it as unconfirmed until read first-hand.
rows.notes: Structural hypothesis: P1481's own endpoints (Ananiv→Bohorodchany) are a literal subset of P1485's endpoints (Kremenchuk→Bohorodchany via Ananiv), same diameter (1020 mm both), similar capacity (9.10 vs 8.70 bcm/y). Moldovatransgaz's own asset registry (fetched verbatim, https://moldovatransgaz.md/... and mirror http://mtg.md/ru/news/54) lists as one of its 8 serviced magistral trunks: '1. Ананьев - Черновцы - Богородчаны (АЧБ) – газопровод, предназначенный для передачи природного газа потребителям Республики Молдова протяженностью 184,8 км, диаметром 1020 мм, с пропускной способностью 9,1 млрд м3 в год'. This confirms 'АЧБ' EXISTS as a distinctly named entity, matching P1481's name near-exactly and its capacity exactly (9.1), and diameter exactly (1020 mm). Separately, TTGPMR (Transnistria's own gas operator, ttgpmr.com/company/history/, institutionally independent of Moldovatransgaz) also names 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bogorodchany' verbatim ('Позже он был соединён 22-километровой перемычкой с газопроводом Ананьев-Черновцы-Богородчаны'), giving a THIRD, independent institutional confirmation the name is real — but none of these three sources states outright whether AChB is (a) the same physical pipe as P1485's western half, described under a Moldovan-side partial name, or (b) a separate parallel string built later in the same corridor. Working against distinctness: the dedicated Ukrainian Wikipedia article on 'Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany' already routes the SAME 532/532.6 km, 1986, 1020 mm trunk through Ananiv → Sholdănești (Moldova, commissioned 1988) → Drochia (Moldova) → Khotyn (Chernivtsi Oblast) → (implied) Bohorodchany — i.e. through the SAME corridor and even the same Chernivtsi-Oblast waypoint (Khotyn) that 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany' names, and when asked directly to check, the article was confirmed to contain NO mention of a second/parallel pipe or thread ('нитка'). That silence, from a dedicated single-pipeline article that otherwise lists individual compressor stations in detail, is meaningful (though not conclusive) evidence for ONE physical trunk under two partial, institution-specific names rather than two physical trunks.

rows.recommendation: FIX regardless of how the duplicate question resolves: 'Gazprom PJSC [100%]' is a confirmed-wrong Owner for this row. Its route (Kremenchuk → Ananiv → Bohorodchany) lies wholly inside Ukraine, and Ukraine's gas transmission system has been Ukrainian-state-owned since independence — operated historically by Naftogaz/JSC Ukrtransgaz and, since 1 Jan 2020, by the Gas TSO of Ukraine (TSOU); Gazprom owns no section of Ukraine's domestic trunkline network. Correct Owner to the Ukrainian state operator, consistent with P1481's own Owner field ('Gas TSO of Ukraine'). ALSO fix the EndLocation inconsistency: EndLocation reads 'Ananiev' but the row's own PipelineName ends at Bohorodchany and its recorded length (532.00 km) matches the FULL Kremenchuk-to-Bohorodchany trunk length reported by independent sources (532/532.6 km) — not a partial Kremenchuk-to-Ananiv leg. EndLocation should read Bohorodchany (or Khotyn/Chernivtsi Oblast if a more precise physical terminus is wanted) to match the sourced full extent. Leave the duplicate-vs-P1481 question open per the cluster note above pending a verbatim primary-source read.
rows.notes: Wikipedia (uk) 'Kremenchuk–Ananiv–Bohorodchany' (verified reachable, https://uk.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%9A%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B5%D0%BD%D1%87%D1%83%D0%BA_%E2%80%93_%D0%90%D0%BD%D0%B0%D0%BD%D1%8C%D1%97%D0%B2_%E2%80%93_%D0%91%D0%BE%D0%B3%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B4%D1%87%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8) confirms, per direct query of the article: length 532 km, diameter 1020 mm, commissioned 1986, capacity toward Bohorodchany 8.7 bcm/y (matches P1485's 8.70 exactly), route Zadniprovska(start)→Kirovohradska→Pivdennobuzka→Ananiv→Sholdănești(Moldova)→Drochia(Moldova)→Khotyn→(Bohorodchany). This is a very close match to P1485's own recorded specs, so its length/diameter/capacity/route are all well corroborated; only Owner and EndLocation are wrong. Search-engine-indexed access to the Ukrtransgaz chronology (utg.ua, direct fetch 403'd, no Wayback capture) independently gives the same 532.6 km/1020 mm/1986 figures, but I could not obtain a verbatim quote to fully verify tier.

summary:
The hypothesis is that P1481 (Ananjiv-Bohorodchani, 333 km, 1020 mm, 9.10 bcm/y, StartYear 1987) is a segment-vs-network double count of P1485 (Kremenchuk-Anan'iv-Bohorodchany, 532 km, 1020 mm, 8.70 bcm/y, StartYear 1985), since P1481's endpoints are a strict subset of P1485's route. After working the source ladder, the evidence is genuinely mixed and I cannot responsibly call this either confirmed or refuted.

What is solid: Moldovatransgaz's own asset registry (fetched verbatim from two live mirrors) lists 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bogorodchany (АЧБ)' as one of 8 distinctly named magistral trunks it services — 184.8 km on Moldovan soil, 1020 mm, 9.1 bcm/y, matching P1481's diameter and capacity exactly. Transnistria's own gas operator (ttgpmr.com, institutionally independent of Moldovatransgaz) independently confirms the name exists. Separately, the dedicated Ukrainian Wikipedia article on 'Kremenchuk-Ananiv-Bohorodchany' gives 532/532.6 km, 1020 mm, 1986, 8.7 bcm/y toward Bohorodchany — matching P1485 closely — and its own compressor-station list ALREADY routes that trunk through Ananiv, two Moldovan stations (Sholdănești, Drochia), and Khotyn (Chernivtsi Oblast) en route to Bohorodchany: i.e. the SAME corridor and the SAME Chernivtsi-Oblast waypoint that 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany' names. When asked directly, that Wikipedia article was confirmed to contain no mention of a second parallel pipe or thread ('нитка'). This pattern — one well-documented trunk whose own route already covers the corridor that a second, Moldovan-side partial name describes — leans toward P1481 being a partial-name re-entry of (part of) P1485, i.e. toward duplication.

What keeps it from being confirmed: the two gatekeeper primary sources that could settle it outright — Ukrtransgaz's own construction chronology (utg.ua) and the Bohorodchanske LVUMG operating-division history (tsoua.com) — both blocked automated fetches (403) with no Wayback capture available. Search-engine indexing gave partial, paraphrase-level access, and on one occasion produced a specific counter-claim (two separately-commissioned 1987-88 pipelines, one of them named 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany', distinct from the 1986 Kremenchuk trunk) that would REFUTE duplication in exactly the Kazakhstan-precedent pattern (parallel Soviet strings) — but a repeat search on similar terms failed to reproduce this claim, so I am not willing to treat it as established. I also found an independent, structural problem with P1481 regardless of the duplicate question: its recorded 333 km length is physically impossible for its own stated endpoints (Ananiv to Bohorodchany are ~424 km apart on a great circle, and no pipe route can be shorter than that), which further erodes confidence in P1481 as a cleanly-documented standalone entity.

Separately, and with full confidence regardless of the duplicate verdict: P1485's Owner field ('Gazprom PJSC [100%]') is a clear attribution error for a wholly-Ukrainian route, and its EndLocation ('Ananiev') is inconsistent with both its own PipelineName and its sourced full 532 km extent to Bohorodchany. Both should be corrected by Update independent of how the duplicate question resolves.
open_questions: Can a verbatim (non-WAF-blocked) copy of the Ukrtransgaz historical chronology (utg.ua) and/or the Bohorodchanske LVUMG chronology page (tsoua.com) be obtained — via a different egress IP, a library database, or a direct ask to TSOU — to settle definitively whether 'Ananiev-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany' is a separately-built 1987-88 line or a Moldovan-side partial name for (part of) the 1986 Kremenchuk trunk?

Where does GEM's P1481 length value of 333.00 km actually come from? It matches neither the 532.6 km whole-trunk figure nor Moldovatransgaz's 184.8 km Moldovan-portion figure for the same-named АЧБ trunk, and is geometrically impossible for its own stated endpoints.

One search pass surfaced a THIRD named line, 'Kremenchuk-Ananiev-Chernivtsi', also reportedly commissioned 1987-88, that does not appear to correspond to any current GEM row in this cluster — worth a quick existence check as a possible Discovery candidate once the AChB question is settled, though it is out of scope for this cluster.
